styles.label: naskh
styles.name: Naskh
styles.period_origin: Codified 10th century CE (Abbasid era) by Ibn Muqla and refined by Ibn al-Bawwab
visual_traits: Small, round proportions with short vertical strokes
Clear letter spacing and moderate contrast between thick and thin strokes
Horizontal baseline with shallow, even curvature
Minimal ligature overlap — each word remains legible in isolation

styles.label: thuluth
styles.name: Thuluth
styles.period_origin: Emerged 8th–9th century CE; codified under the Abbasids and perfected by Ottoman masters
visual_traits: Large, sweeping curved letters with pronounced vertical alifs
Heavy overlapping of letters and words along a rising-and-falling line
Strong contrast between broad downstrokes and hairline connectors
Frequent stacked compositions where letters interlace above the baseline
common_use_cases: Royal seals, coins, and ceremonial calligraphic panels (levha)

styles.label: diwani
styles.name: Diwani
styles.period_origin: Developed 16th century CE in the Ottoman imperial chancery under Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent
visual_traits: Extremely cursive with steep diagonal slanting lines
Letters tightly interlocked into dense, often unreadable-to-laymen clusters
Elaborate flourishes and dot ornaments crowning word groups
Jali variant fills counters with decorative knotwork
common_use_cases: Decorative panels, logos, and state emblems

styles.label: kufi
styles.name: Kufi
styles.period_origin: Oldest monumental Arabic script, formalized 7th–8th century CE around Kufa, Iraq
visual_traits: Angular, rectilinear letterforms built on square or geometric grids
Long horizontal extensions with minimal ascenders or curves
Early manuscripts lack vowel marks and even some letter differentiation
Ornamental variants: foliated, floriated, braided, and brick-style Kufic
common_use_cases: Architectural band inscriptions on mosques and monuments
Modern logotypes, flags, and abstract art

styles.label: ruqah
styles.name: Ruqʿah
styles.period_origin: Evolved 17th century CE from taʿliq in Ottoman scribal practice
visual_traits: Compact letters written on a straight baseline with a slight rightward lean
Words frequently descend below the baseline in stepped clusters
Dots and short vowel strokes are reduced or omitted for speed
Letters are simplified and connected with blunt, functional joins
common_use_cases: Everyday handwriting across the Arab world

styles.label: modern
styles.name: Modern / Contemporary
styles.period_origin: 20th century CE onward, following the Nahda and the Hurufiyya art movement
visual_traits: Simplified letterforms adapted from naskh for legibility at scale
Free mixing of historical scripts with abstract or geometric treatment
Sans-serif digital proportions; baseline rules deliberately broken
Decorative elements borrowed freely across classical styles
common_use_cases: Book covers, posters, and media graphics
